frontiers.target: Scan Turbo C++ 1.00 libraries for exact library contributions
frontiers.state: closed for CS.LIB (small model); other models confirmed contributing nothing
frontiers.matches: tools/library_scanner.py generalized the STARTUP_C0S match-modulo-fixups technique across CS.LIB's 312 member modules (anchored on census function boundaries, with a memmem fallback requiring uniqueness). Found 42 exact matches (2732 bytes, file offsets 0x9613-0xb49b: ATEXIT, CLOSE, FFLUSH, FLUSHALL, WRITE, READ, MEMCPY, MEMSET, STRCPY, INPORT, OUTPORT, long-arithmetic helpers, etc.), most laid out back-to-back exactly as real linked runtime code -- strong structural evidence, not coincidence. All promoted to KNOWN_LIBRARY. CC/CM/CL/CH.LIB (other memory models) confirmed to contribute nothing further, consistent with the small-model finding.
frontiers.unblock: Re-run against newly-classified RAW_UNKNOWN regions as more of the code segment is mapped -- this is not a one-shot scan, revisit periodically (tracked as a lightweight follow-up under the function-census frontier, not a separate blocker).
frontiers.leverage: 3301 of the manifest's 3339 non-code-metadata classified bytes so far came from this technique -- the single highest-yield mechanical step used to date.

frontiers.matches: Format fully determined: uint32 resource count (401) + offset table, two resource kinds by size (FIXED_TILE_16x16, 128 bytes; SPRITE_VAR, variable with a 4-byte width/height header, padded width rounded to a multiple of 8, always declared_height+1 stored rows), 4 EGA bitplanes in I,R,G,B order MSB-first, standard 16-color EGA/CGA palette. Visually confirmed via rendered PNGs (recognizable tiles and Dave sprite frames) and cross-checked against public ModdingWiki documentation. tools/egadave_decode.py / tools/egadave_encode.py round-trip the ENTIRE file exactly: re-encoded MD5 == 15e4cfe305600a8acd39d4bc7fe9c591, zero raw fallbacks.

frontiers.target: First matching-C promotion inside actual game code
frontiers.state: one function landed; this frontier stays open under a new name for further promotions
frontiers.matches: F_6D64 (file offset [0x6d64,0x6d8a), 38 bytes): a compiled switch(param) dispatch head (4-case jump table via near-to-far pointer setup). src/F_6D64.c reproduces the declared extent byte-for-byte with zero unexplained differences (only fixup-covered bytes differ). Honestly scoped: the case-body content in the source is explicitly documented as a placeholder chosen only to make the non-fixup branch displacement byte match -- only the 38-byte dispatch head is claimed, not the case bodies/jump table that follow (file offset ~0x6d8a-0x6dba), which remain RAW_UNKNOWN. New reusable tool tools/match_function.py (candidate.c -> compile -> OMF -> bind fixups -> full-extent byte compare) generalizes tools/recover_startup_binding.py's proof standard for arbitrary candidate functions, not just library modules.
frontiers.unblock: See 'Continue matching-C promotions' below for the ongoing frontier this seeds.
frontiers.leverage: Proves the full promotion loop (tools/match_function.py) end-to-end on real game code, not just linked-in library code -- the central methodology this whole project phase depends on.

frontiers.target: Import and verify yo-yo-yo-jbo/dangerous_dave RE facts
frontiers.state: closed for the 10 facts checked; revisit if the external project adds more
frontiers.matches: docs/external-re-evidence.json: fetched the external repo, independently re-hashed its own committed DAVE.EXE (not trusted from its README), and documented that it mixes three different unlabeled address conventions (literal file offsets, IDA sub_ addresses needing -0x10000 then +0x200, raw DS-relative word_ operands). Of 10 imported facts: 7 verified instruction-for-instruction (game-init function, level-completion dispatcher, warp-transition function, score/lives-cap logic, two data tables), 2 contradicted, 1 could_not_check. Every verified fact's address was already present in our own call-graph census -- a strong two-way cross-check.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: One contradiction is substantive and unresolved: the external project's claimed g_levels base address (file offset 0x26E0A) is wrong -- that offset is a text string ('ENTER FILENAME...'-style prompt) in our bytes, and is arithmetically inconsistent with the SAME external project's own separately-verified level-6 warp-bug address. The true base of g_levels has not yet been independently re-derived by this project.
frontiers.unblock: Independently re-derive g_levels' real base address (e.g. by tracing data references from the level-loading function this import identified) rather than trusting either project's unverified guess -- tracked as its own frontier below.
frontiers.leverage: Surfaced 4 new semantically-identified matching-C candidates with known purpose (game-init/level-completion and related functions), not just address boundaries -- a significant accelerant for the matching-C queue.

end_state: Independent source modules (matching C, matching ASM, structured data/assets) compile, assemble, and link with a historically faithful toolchain such that the resulting unpacked executable image is byte-identical to the original, addresses emerge from module composition rather than being copied, and the image can subsequently be re-packed with LZEXE 0.91 to reproduce the original DAVE.EXE exactly. EGADAVE.DAV resources are simultaneously reconstructed from human-readable canonical sources (images, tables) plus deterministic encoders.
